phosphorus-cycle.def: The movement of phosphorus among rock, soil, water, sediments and living things. It has no significant gas phase, so it is slow; weathering, uptake, decomposition and sedimentation move it.

weathering.def: The breakdown of rock into smaller pieces and dissolved minerals by water, ice, temperature changes, chemical reactions and living things. It releases phosphate and other nutrients into soil.

phosphate.def: The form of phosphorus (PO4 with a negative charge) that plants take up and that makes up DNA, ATP, cell membranes, and bones and teeth. It clings to soil particles.
